summary: PulseGuard v0.6.25 fixes post-fix health scoring and report preservation, makes WinGet/optimizer history survive the background rescan, and stops normal locked cache files from being reported as Deep Clean warnings.

sections.heading: Post-fix health score now uses only new crash evidence
sections.detail: Repeated-application rows in Event Viewer are 30-day aggregates. PulseGuard now re-counts crashes after the verified-fix watermark instead of relabeling the entire historical total as current when one newer event appears. A Windows component or app only remains a repeated current fault after 3 or more new crashes occur after the verified fix.

sections.heading: sppsvc history no longer resurrects after classification changes
sections.detail: Windows Software Protection (sppsvc.exe) now shares the same resolved-event history key used by the earlier Application Stability classification. Old retained crash records stay visible as history but do not keep subtracting health-score points after a verified fix unless the component actually begins repeating again.

sections.heading: Post-fix reports preserve WinGet and optimization evidence
sections.detail: The Full Health Scan runs in a background PowerShell worker, which does not share the parent UI process's optimization memory. PulseGuard now regenerates the consolidated report in the parent process after importing the fresh scan, preserving OptimizationSteps, OptimizationChanges, before/after snapshots, WinGet results, Deep Clean results, registry/privacy evidence, and other current-session maintenance data.

sections.heading: Deep Clean safe skips are no longer warnings
sections.detail: Live browser, DirectX, iCUE, and other disposable cache files that are locked or access-protected by running applications are now recorded as safely skipped rather than cleanup errors. Deep Clean separately reports deleted items, freed space, safely skipped active files, and real cleanup errors. Safe skips do not turn FIX + OPTIMIZE ALL into a warning.

sections.heading: Cleaner and registry wording is clearer
sections.detail: Deep Clean preview items are described as candidates because running applications may keep some cache files open. Registry review-only evidence is explicitly labeled protected/review-only and does not imply that a repair failed or that the health score should be reduced.

sections.heading: WinGet visibility retained
sections.detail: The WinGet application-update Command Prompt is explicitly launched as a normal elevated window, stays open for the full winget upgrade --all run, then keeps the completed result visible for 5 seconds before closing automatically.
